we have developed a qualitative study of the energy eigenvalues of a nanotubes model under the influence of an external magnetic fields using an iterative Taylor approximation.
the energy spectrum of a model of graphene nanotube under a uniform magnetic field, obtained from an exact solution, splits into two different ones for nontrivial values of the parameter kx.

the development and application of an efficient method of solving a Dirac–Weyn equation in a model of graphene nanotube under the presence of a magnetic field.
the study of a nanomodel under the presence of external fields.
the development of an efficient numerical method to obtain the eigenvalues of a model of graphene nanotube under the influence of an external field.

the model is not a trivial one, but it is a model that deserves to be studied in depth.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the energy spectrum for a graphene nanotube under the presence of a magnetic field is not continuous, but it is composed by some bands separated by some gaps, as it occurs for the electronic structure of solids in the presence of an electric field.
, in general, the energy spectrum of a nanotubes is not continuous, and it is strongly influenced by the value of the parameter kz.
, in general, the energy eigenvalues are not degenerate, and that the degenerate energy levels are not necessarily the minimal ones.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the presence of the parameter kz, which cannot be neglected in a physical model, produces gaps in the energy levels.
, for nontrivial values of kz, the energy gaps in the spectrum are not closed.
the energy spectrum of the model depends on kz.
